subject: Low call rate and very low loci after filtering

messages.author: 29c83983c63ac71c
messages.subject: Low call rate and very low loci after filtering
parts:
Hi,

I have 94 individuals of an annual daisy collected across 12 populations (~8 indiv. per population). These populations are spread across isolated remnants along a 150 km sampling transect. For SNP data, individuals missing data range from 0.23 to 0.63, reporting call rate by individual yields ~32,000 loci (median call rate ~0.44). After filtering for secondaries with a threashold of 0.9, I ended up with 329 loci. While doing a PCoA on this, the axes explain combined ~5%.

This is my first time using SNP data and DArT and my results are very different colleagues doing similar work. We sent the samples for DNA extraction and sequencing and I am wondering if this is a problem with low DNA quality/extraction issues or whether it is a problem with the species? Any advice you have would be greatly appreciated.

Manuel

messages.author: d87216285ace7535
messages.subject: Re: [dartR] Low call rate and very low loci after filtering
parts:
The only way to really know is to ask DArT for their advice on the
quality of the DNA extracted or any other issues they had. They take
pictures of every step so it is all very carefully documented.

When you plot missing loci do you get an even looking plot, or something
bimodal looking (i.e., multiple peaks)?

I would also try doing a light filtering and running a tree to check
that you don't have some quirky samples in there that might be quite
different. Tree type analyses aren't as impacted by missing data.
Usually you can get away with running a neighbour joining tree (although
sometimes these can produce quirky results, but usually they are okay).

Cheers
Peter Unmack

messages.author: 592079bda2cb3220
messages.subject: Re: [dartR] Low call rate and very low loci after filtering
parts:
Hi Manuel,

Thanks for sharing the list of filters you used (see below).

gl_waitzia <- gl.filter.callrate(gl_waitzia, method = "loc", threshold = 0.95)
gl_waitzia <- gl.filter.rdepth(gl_waitzia, lower = 10, upper = 100)
gl_waitzia <- gl.filter.reproducibility(gl_waitzia, threshold = 0.99)
gl_waitzia <- gl.filter.monomorphs(gl_waitzia)

Your filter thresholds are not that stringent, but you ended up with quite a few loci. It is likely that your samples had a low quantity/quality DNA. As Peter mentioned, you could ask DArT for a summary of the DNA of your samples. 

However, if you use less stringent thresholds, you will still get good quality SNPs. For example, you could use a minimum threshold for read depth of 5 and not using an upper threshold or using a call rate of 0.80. You could also first filter those samples with the most missing data and then filter missing data by loci. 

You can find more information on filtering on our tutorials:

- Microsoft Word - Tutorial_5_dartR_Basic_Filtering_22-Dec-21 (2).doc (biomatix.org)
- Session 2 Renee Catullo (youtube.com)
- Kioloa PopGen - 1  Intro to dartR (green-striped-gecko.github.io)

You could also impute your missing data by using the function gl.impute. 

What's more important, though, is to understand the implications of missing data and number of loci for each of the analyses you will perform. 

Cheers,
Luis
